note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 6af25a7a79). Appendix A.4.7: "It MUST NOT be set to the IPv6 Unspecified Address (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0) or an IPv6 Link-Local Address (Prefix FE80/10)." and "While OSPFv3 routes are normally installed with link-local addresses, an OSPFv3 implementation advertising a forwarding address MUST advertise a global IPv6 address." 6af25a7a79 touched only rfc/discrimination/rfc5340.json: the translator negative's record moves from a panic of v6UsableForwardingAddress (reach only) to the mutant at interface_addr.go:73 dropping '!addr.IsLinkLocalUnicast() &&'. Line 73 at HEAD is that return statement, and with the link-local term gone fe80::2/fe80::3 pass every remaining term (Is6, not 4in6, not loopback, unspecified or multicast), so translatableForwardingAddressV6 admits it and the negative's 'no Type-5' assertion is the one that fails, as the author reports (red at :60/:77, not re-observed here). This closes the prior judge's note that the record proved reach, not the branch. Producers, tests and claims are byte-identical to the last judgement; tagged units pass at HEAD (go test -count=1). For -1: TestRFC5340TranslatorNeverAdvertisesLinkLocalForwarding asserts a global address is carried unchanged and fe80::2 yields no Type-5; the Unspecified half is pinned by TestRFC5340ForwardingAddressIsGlobal (:: refused, all-zero origination clears HasForwardingAddr), and translateNSSAV6 skips an all-zero forwarding address before the gate.
